No new ideas today: three short problems that use Lectures 10, 11 and 12 on
the level generator of a game. Do each one alone, then open "Check your
result". Every question on this page has its answer: try first, then check.

## Recall

- The same seed gives the same random numbers (Lecture 11). A success with
  probability p takes 1/p tries on average (Lecture 10).
- E = x₁p₁ + x₂p₂ + …: the long-run average per try (Lecture 10).
- A shuffle bag keeps the shares and spreads the results evenly
  (Lecture 12).

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Recall"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="a new seed|20"}
A tester wants to see the same random numbers again. What does the tester need?
:   the same seed

    Why: the same seed and the same code give the same numbers.

A rule allows 50 % of the tiles. How many draws are needed on average?
:   2

    Why: 1/p = 1/0.5.

A room gives 10 coins with p = 0.3, else nothing. What is E per room?
:   3

    Why: 10 × 0.3.
:::
:::

## Activity 1 · The same seed, the same cave

*Torch Hall* makes a new cave for every floor. It starts with walls
everywhere. A walker starts in the middle and moves one random step at a
time; every tile it steps on becomes floor. The exit goes on the floor tile
farthest from the start. All its random numbers come from one seed.

![The same seed gives the same level.](images/seeds.png){width=86%}

{{< sim file="sims/cave-gen.html" poster="sims/cave-gen.png" title="Cave Generator: one seed, one level" height="760" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 1 · Seeds and steps · 15 min"}
1. In **Cave Generator**, write where the chest is with seed 42. Go to seed
   43, then back to 42. What stays the same?
2. A tester finds a bug on one floor. What must the tester write in the
   report? How can all players get the same floor today?
3. The walker makes 20 steps. At most how many new floor tiles can it make?
   Why are there often fewer?

*Your product:* three short answers, each with a reason.

::: {.check}
1. Everything stays the same with seed 42: the walls, the start, the exit
   and the chest.
2. The seed of the floor: with it the team makes the same floor again. A
   shared daily seed gives every player the same floor.
3. At most 20; often fewer, because the walker steps on some tiles again.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Seeds and steps"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="a faster CPU|0"}
How does the game make a new floor every time?
:   a new seed, for example from the time

    Why: a new seed gives new random numbers.

Why is a walker cave always one connected piece?
:   the walker moves only to a neighbour tile

    Why: every new tile touches the tile before it.

The walker makes 30 steps. At most how many new floor tiles does it make?
:   30

    Why: one tile per step at most; repeated tiles add nothing.
:::
:::

## Activity 2 · A monster and the rooms

A monster must not stand within 3 steps of the start, so the game draws a
random floor tile and draws again when the rule fails; 80 % of the tiles
are allowed. Each room gets an event from a table: a chest with 25 %
(+20 coins), a torch with 5 % (+100 coins), and nothing with 70 %. A floor
has 8 rooms. The team compares the table with a shuffle bag of the same
shares.

![An event table: each event with its probability and its reward.](images/event-table.png){width=86%}

{{< sim file="sims/event-deck.html" poster="sims/event-deck.png" title="Event Deck: what is in each room?" height="560" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 2 · Draws, coins and a bag · 20 min"}
1. How many draws does the monster need on average?
2. Find the expected coins per room and per floor of 8 rooms.
3. Find P(no chest in 2 rooms), with the table.
4. In **Event Deck**, test 1000 floors with the table, then with the bag.
   Compare the coins per floor and the floors without a chest.

*Your product:* one number of draws, two expected values, one probability
and one sentence on the bag.

::: {.check}
1. 1/0.8 = 1.25 draws.
2. E = 20 × 0.25 + 100 × 0.05 + 0 = 5 + 5 = 10 coins per room; 80 coins
   per floor.
3. 0.75 × 0.75 = 0.5625, about 56 %.
4. Both methods give about 80 coins per floor; the bag has far fewer floors
   without a chest: it spreads the chests but keeps the shares.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Rooms"}
Empty 60 %, chest 30 % (+10 coins), torch 10 % (+50 coins). Choose the
right answer.

::: {.match extra="25|100"}
What is the expected number of coins per room?
:   8

    Why: 10 × 0.3 + 50 × 0.1 = 3 + 5.

What is the expected number of coins for 6 rooms?
:   48

    Why: 6 × 8.

What does a shuffle bag change?
:   fewer unlucky floors, the same shares

    Why: the bag keeps the shares and spreads the results.
:::
:::

## Activity 3 · The reports of the testers

The testers of *Torch Hall* send six reports. A player wants a friend to play
the same floor. A new monster rule allows 80 % of the tiles. A room holds a
chest with 20 % (+30 coins) or a gem with 10 % (+50 coins); a floor has 10
rooms, and some floors have no gem at all. A new rule puts the exit at least
20 steps from the start.

![Test a generator with many seeds: look at the average and at the extremes.](images/generator-test.png){width=86%}

{{< sim file="sims/generator-doctor.html" poster="sims/generator-doctor.png" title="Generator Doctor: six reports about the generator" kind="game" height="460" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Activity 3 · Answer the reports · 20 min"}
1. What does the player share with the friend?
2. Find the expected draws for the monster, and the expected coins per room
   and per floor.
3. P(no gem in a room) = 0.9; for 10 rooms it is 0.9¹⁰ ≈ 0.35. Which change
   gives every floor gems at the same rate?
4. After the exit rule changes, what does the team do? Then play
   **Generator Doctor** and answer the six reports.

*Your product:* four short answers and your score in Generator Doctor.

::: {.check}
1. The seed of the floor.
2. 1/0.8 = 1.25 draws. E = 30 × 0.2 + 50 × 0.1 = 6 + 5 = 11 coins per room;
   110 coins per floor.
3. About 35 % of the floors have no gem. A shuffle bag with 1 gem in every 10
   rooms gives each floor its gem and keeps the rate.
4. Test again with 1000 seeds or more and compare the path lengths with the
   old rule: the average and the extremes.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Reports"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="1|never"}
A problem appears on 0.5 % of the seeds. About how often in 1000 seeds?
:   about 5 times

    Why: 1000 × 0.005 = 5.

About how many seeds does a good test need?
:   1000 or more

    Why: a rare problem shows up only with many seeds.

Besides the average, what does the team look at?
:   the extremes

    Why: a few very short or very long paths can spoil a floor.
:::
:::

## Wrap-up {.summary}

- You can repeat or share a random level with its seed.
- You can find the expected draws and coins of a generator, and choose a
  shuffle bag for fairer floors.
- You can plan a test of a generator with many seeds.
